chunks: And from him from Ali ibn Asbat from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the alms-tax of wealth, and he said: 'It is obligatory in nine things; there is nothing in others. [It is obligatory] in gold and silver, wheat, barley, dates, raisins, camels, cattle, and grazing sheep (which are the grazing ones). And there is nothing in any of the animals other than these three categories. And for everything that is from these three categories, there is nothing [obligatory] until a year passes over it, from the day it is weaned.'
In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful; and to Him belongs all praise, and by Him we seek help.

key_terms.السَّائِمَةُ: Grazing (animals that feed on natural pasture)
key_terms.يَحُولَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَوْلُ: The passing of a full year

ai.seo_question: What are the nine specific types of wealth subject to zakat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) delineates the nine primary categories of wealth subject to zakat, establishing a clear distinction between specific livestock (camels, cattle, and grazing sheep) and other animals. It further clarifies the temporal condition for obligation, stating that the lunar year (hawl) begins counting from the moment the asset is weaned or acquired, a nuance critical in Shia jurisprudence for determining the precise timing of zakat liability.
